title: Lavender Tallow Balm: I Tried Beef Fat on My Face and It Worked
body:
Okay so. My skin was just being difficult this spring. Like, more than usual. I was using that La Roche-Posay stuff, the one in the blue bottle that’s like thirty bucks, and my cheeks were still tight. Felt like paper. I’d wake up and they’d be flaky. It was annoying. I was scrolling through Etsy one night, probably too late, and I saw this thing. A whipped tallow balm. Lavender. Made in France. I stared at it. Beef fat. For your face. I mean, come on. But the description said it was grass-fed, whipped into this… thing. Mimics your skin’s oil. For dry skin, eczema, all that. I was skeptical. Obviously. But my skin was so mad at me. And it was spring, but it felt like winter on my face. So I bought it. The Whipped Tallow Balm with lavender. I figured, worst case, I waste some money and have a weird story.

Here’s the thing about my old routine. It was a whole production. Cleanse, tone, serum, moisturizer, eye cream. All from Sephora. Probably two hundred dollars worth of bottles on my sink. And my skin? Fine. Just fine. Not great. Not terrible. Just… beige. It existed. But this spring, the dryness kicked in hard. My elbows were rough. My knuckles looked cracked. I felt like a lizard. I was putting that CeraVe Healing Ointment on my lips every night, the one in the big tub, and it helped but it was so greasy. I’d get it on my pillow. My cat would look at me like I was disgusting. She’s judgy.

So the tallow balm showed up. Small jar. Simple label. I opened it.

## How I Started Putting Tallow on My Face

First impression: It looked like butter. Whipped butter. I poked it. Texture was weird. Not bad weird. Thick, but soft. I put a tiny bit on my finger. It was cool. Then it warmed up real fast from my skin. I don’t know how to describe it. It just melted. Smelled like lavender. Not like a candle. Not like soap. Just… lavender. Like the plant. Maybe a little earthy underneath? Or not. Something. I was standing in my bathroom, in my socks, thinking “I am about to rub cow fat into my face.” It felt very primal. Or stupid. One of those.

I did it anyway. After I washed my face. Just a little scoop. Rubbed it between my palms and then patted it on. My face felt… shiny. Not oily, but like, protected. It soaked in pretty quick though. Within a few minutes it wasn’t shiny anymore. It just felt like my skin, but quieter. Does that make sense? Like the tight, papery feeling was gone. It was just calm. I went to bed thinking it would clog my pores and I’d wake up with a million little bumps.

I didn’t.

I woke up and my face was… fine. Really fine. Soft. Not greasy. The flakiness on my cheeks was gone. Just gone. I was shocked. I kept using it. Just at night. As my night cream. My whole natural skincare routine became: wash face, tallow balm. That’s it. I stopped with the serum. Stopped with the fancy moisturizer. My sink looked emptier. My wallet felt happier.

## Why Beef Tallow for Skin Actually Makes Sense

I got curious after a week. Why did this work? So I read a little. Not a deep dive, just some articles while I drank my coffee. Apparently, tallow from grass-fed cows is really similar to the oils our own skin makes. Our sebum. So it absorbs deep. It doesn’t just sit on top like a silicone barrier. It tells your skin it can chill out, stop over-producing oil or getting so dry. It’s like giving your skin what it actually recognizes. Not some lab-created chemical with a fancy name.

That clicked for me. All those expensive bottles were full of stuff my skin didn’t know what to do with. This was simple. Beef fat, whipped with some lavender oil for smell. That’s it. It’s good for super dry spots, eczema, chapped lips… I tried it on my elbows and they smoothed out in like, two days. I used it on my lips instead of the CeraVe and it worked better. No greasy pillow. My cat was less judgy.

I started using it daily. Not just at night. A tiny bit in the morning too, under my sunscreen. It became my one thing. My tallow balm daily use thing. Switching to natural products felt less like a trendy choice and more like a “oh, this just works better” choice. I didn’t have to think about it.

## My Skin After a Few Weeks of This Stuff

So it’s been a few weeks now. Maybe a month? I lost track. I’m bad with time. It was a Tuesday when I ordered it I think.

My skin isn’t “perfect.” I didn’t have a dramatic transformation. I still get a stress pimple sometimes. But the overall texture is different. It’s just… even. Hydrated. It doesn’t freak out when the weather changes. That tight, itchy feeling is gone. My face doesn’t feel like a separate entity I have to manage. It just feels like my face. That’s the real result. It’s not glowing like a diamond or whatever. It’s just healthy. Normal. Comfortable.

I told my mom about it. She has eczema on her hands. Really bad. I gave her my jar to try. She called me two days later and said her knuckles weren’t cracked anymore. She ordered her own. I’m on my second jar now. I got it from the same little Etsy shop, **Saint Fiacre**. The shipping was fast again. It’s just a small operation, I think. Makes it feel like you found a secret.

The lavender scent is calming. It’s not overpowering. It’s just there. Makes the whole before-bed thing feel like a ritual. Wash face, pat on the balm, smell the lavender, and that’s it. My brain associates it with sleep now. It’s good for anxiety relief, I guess, just because the routine is so simple. No chaos. No ten-step process. Just one thing that works.

## Would I Buy This Lavender Tallow Balm Again?

Yeah. I already did.

Look, I’m not a skincare guru. I’m just a person whose skin was being difficult. I tried a weird thing—putting whipped beef tallow on my face—and the weird thing worked better than all the normal, expensive things. I don’t know what else to say about it. It absorbs. It doesn’t clog my pores. It fixed my dry patches. My skin is happy. I’m happy. That’s all I wanted.

If you’re curious about switching to a natural skincare routine and you have dry, fussy skin… this might be worth a shot. It’s one of those things you just have to try to get it. It sounds gross but it’s not. It’s just simple. And sometimes simple is what actually works.

Anyway. My second jar is half empty. I’ll probably order another one soon.

---

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Yeah, surprisingly. From what I read, the fat from grass-fed cows is really close to the oils our own skin makes. So it absorbs deep and helps your skin balance itself out. It’s not just greasing you up.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
Hasn’t clogged mine. And my skin can get clogged easy. Because it’s so similar to our sebum, it seems to sink in instead of sitting on top and blocking stuff. My pores look fine. Better, even.

**What does the lavender tallow balm smell like?**
Just like lavender. The real plant. Not fake or perfume-y. It’s earthy and herbal. It’s calming. It’s not strong, just a nice scent that fades after you rub it in. Makes putting it on at night feel kinda nice.

So yeah. If your skin is being difficult, might be worth a shot.
